title: Config-aware Shadow Evaluations to Detect Typed JSON Regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a low-latency, config-aware 'shadow evaluation' pipeline that continuously runs production-like requests through candidate model/config variants and detects regressions in typed JSON outputs (schema compliance, type mismatches, missing/extra fields, field-level distribution shifts). This feature complements existing canary rollouts by providing higher-sensitivity signal tied to config changes (quantization profiles, kernel selection, batching policies) and model swaps before traffic is shifted.

Scope and constraints:
- Shadow runs must not add >5% tail latency risk to production paths; completely decoupled execution preferred (async fork + best-effort sampling).
- Support multiple schema sources: static JSON schemas in repo, per-route typed contracts published by PM, and on-the-fly inference-based schema hints.
- Detect both syntactic (invalid JSON, schema violations) and semantic regressions (field type flips, consistent numeric truncation, enum drift).
- Provide per-field metrics (violation rate, KL divergence for distributions, median token length) and aggregated stability score.

Design overview:
1) Ingress sampling: traffic mirror at the routing layer samples 2% of requests for shadow evaluation. Sample rate configurable per-route and per-customer.
2) Execution: sampled requests are forked to a shadow runner pool that can use alternative model versions and runtime configs. Shadow runner returns full token stream and parsed JSON candidate.
3) Normalization: apply canonicalization hooks (whitespace, ordering, ID normalization) and map outputs into typed field buckets for comparison.
4) Metrics: compute field-level failure types (missing, extra, type_mismatch, enum_unrecognised), numeric distribution deltas (Wasserstein), string similarity histograms, and parse-failure counts.
5) Alerting and gating: define short-window (1h) and long-window (7d) thresholds; integrate with Console to show a stability score and trigger rollout block/fallback when a configurable P0 threshold is exceeded.
6) Storage and retention: keep example pairs (request + golden + candidate) for 90 days for debugging, with redaction rules for PII.

Automation & integration:
- On config change (runtime profile/quantization/batching), create an automated shadow-eval job that runs on the new config for a 24h warmup collecting baseline metrics; compare to the pinned baseline using bootstrapped significance tests.
- Integrate with rollout engine to add a pre-rollout check; if shadow-eval reports regression above threshold, abort canary and notify owners with a diagnostic bundle.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds (initial):
- Field schema violation rate > 0.5% in 1h window => warning.
- Any high-severity required-field drop (missing required field present in golden) > 0.05% => immediate block.
- Parse failures (invalid JSON) > 0.01% => immediate block.
- Per-field KL or Wasserstein delta > adaptive threshold (based on sample variance) => signal for manual review.

Observability and developer UX:
- Console dashboard per-route and per-config showing stability score, top failing fields, example request/candidate pairs, and time-series for violation types.
- One-click download of diagnostic bundle (10k examples max) and links to related PRs, deployment configs, and reproduced failing traces.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (spike): prototype mirror + minimal parser + dashboard (dev cluster).
- Week 2: expand sample hooks, add canonicalizers, integrate with Console metrics.
- Week 3: automated pre-rollout check coupled to runtime config changes; alert rules and runbook.
- Week 4: beta with two internal teams (Docs AI and Search) and iterate on thresholds.

Risks & mitigations:
- Noise from nondeterministic outputs: use stable-canonicalization and ensemble baselines; consider sampling by user cohort to control variability.
- Storage costs for examples: enforce TTL and sample deduplication; redact large blobs.
- False positives from schema underspecification: provide tooling for PMs/Designers to mark optional/ignored fields and supply model-tolerant schemas.

Success criteria (30 days post-beta):
- Detect at least two real regressions that would have otherwise escalated in canary.
- Average time-to-detect for schema breakages < 2 hours after config/model change.
- Console adoption: two product teams using stability dashboard during rollouts.

2025-02-18 — Design review with PM/Design: decided to support both static JSON schema and lightweight inferred schema to reduce onboarding friction. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Config-Aware+Shadow+Eval

2025-02-21 — Metric prototypes landed: per-field violation counter and parse-failure alert (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/128). Need to harden canonicalizers for IDs and timestamps.

2025-02-26 — Integration note: added automated job trigger on config changes in gitops pipeline (see pipeline PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/99). Still blocked on KMS redaction policy review (security).

2025-03-01 — Working with Console team on dashboard widgets; draft panels available at Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/xxxx/shadow-eval-overview. Preparing beta rollout with Docs AI team for next cycle.
